title: Problem statement confirmation
question: Is the target the retained memory after the call (not the peak), and is the fix a library setting so the caller does not touch GINu/GINc?

options.text: Confirm both points
Correct the statement

decision: Target is retained memory after the call. Fix is a library setting.

title: API shape
question: How does a caller ask for an encoder that the library builds for one call and drops?

options.text: Third profile value on the existing EncoderProfile enum. Reuses WithEncoderProfile and WithEncodeProfile. Always one worker plus low-memory buffers. No invalid combinations. Enum then mixes two ideas: worker count and retention.

Separate retention option (config option plus per-call twin). Keeps the two ideas apart. Needs a rule for default profile plus uncached: reject with an error, or force one worker. 2 new options and 1 new GINConfig field.

Package function that empties the shared encoder cache (for example ReleaseEncoders). Also frees default-profile encoders. Global and racy with other goroutines. The cache still gets an entry, so it does not meet the issue text.

rationale: Fact F5 makes uncached sensible only with one worker, so option B has one legal combination and is a profile in disguise. A flows through Parquet, sidecar and S3 with no new plumbing (F7).
decision: Third profile value on the existing EncoderProfile enum.

title: Concurrent calls
question: N goroutines that encode at the same time each build their own encoder, so the peak is N x 44 MB at level 15. The cached bounded-memory profile queues them on one worker instead. What does the library do?

options.text: Document only. The caller limits its own concurrency. State the N x 44 MB cost in the godoc and README.
Add a package-level limit so only one uncached encoder exists at a time. Calls wait in line. Peak stays near 44 MB but adds hidden blocking and context-cancel handling.

rationale: The target user is a batch job that encodes one index per batch. A limiter is new behavior that the issue does not ask for.
decision: Document the N x 44 MB cost. No limiter in the library.

title: Meaning of peak in the doc row
question: The issue asks for a doc row with peak, retained and construction time. The doc has no peak column today. Which number do we publish as peak?

options.text: Alloc/op from the existing cold benchmark, labelled as bytes allocated per call. Upper bound for the live peak. Same method as the rest of the doc. No new measuring code.
Sampled live-heap peak with runtime/metrics during the encode. Closer to the true peak. New measuring code, and a sampler can miss a short peak.
cgroup memory.peak from a subprocess on Linux. The number an operator sees. Linux only, needs a new test program.

rationale: The issue itself says the peak is the same with and without retention. The numbers that separate the new row are retained and construction time. A is honest if the column label says allocated per call.
decision: Publish Alloc/op from the cold benchmark, labelled as allocated per call.

title: Host for the new doc numbers
question: The doc numbers came from a linux/amd64 host with klauspost v1.19.2. This machine is darwin/arm64 and go.mod pins v1.20.0. Where do the new numbers come from?

options.text: New section in the doc with its own host header. Measure cached bounded-memory and uncached side by side on this machine. Leave the old tables as they are.
Run the full benchmark again on this machine and replace all tables. One consistent host, but every published number changes.
The implementation adds the benchmark. The maintainer runs make bench-encoder-profile on the original linux/amd64 host and supplies the output.

rationale: A compares the two modes on one host, which is the comparison the reader needs, and does not rewrite numbers that PR 80 published.
decision: New doc section with its own host line, cached bounded-memory and uncached measured together on this machine. Old tables unchanged.

title: Shared decoder
question: The shared zstd decoder is also kept for the process life and its retained size is not measured (F9). Issue 83 is about encoding only. What do we do?

options.text: Out of scope. Record it in the task's deferred items. No GitHub issue.
Out of scope, and I open a follow-up GitHub issue to measure it.
In scope: measure it now and add the number to the doc.

rationale: No one reported a decoder problem. A batch job that only writes indexes never builds the decoder.
decision: Decoder is out of scope. Recorded as a deferred item. The words "file a follow up" are ambiguous between a deferred item and a GitHub issue; clarified in Q8.

title: Public name of the new profile
question: What is the constant name and its String() text?

options.text: EncoderProfileBoundedMemoryUncached, String() "bounded-memory-uncached". Name from the issue. Says both facts: same encoder shape as bounded-memory, not in the cache. Sorts next to its sibling in editor completion. Long (35 characters).
EncoderProfileTransient, String() "transient". Short. Does not say that it is one worker with low memory; the reader must open the godoc.
EncoderProfileBoundedMemoryOneShot, String() "bounded-memory-one-shot". Describes the life of the encoder (one call) and not the cache, which is an internal detail.

rationale: The code and the benchmark doc already use the word uncached for this exact encoder (newZstdEncoder comment). A public constant cannot be renamed later without a breaking change, so the name that needs no explanation is the safer one.

title: Strength of the no-encoder-stays-reachable test
question: How does the test show that no encoder stays reachable after the call?

options.text: Two checks, no change to production code for the test: (1) the shared encoder cache has no entry for the new profile and no new bounded-memory entry after the call; (2) live heap after GC grows by less than a coarse limit (for example 8 MB, against 42 MB if the encoder stayed). This is the literal wording of the acceptance item.

A plus a direct check: an unexported hook in serialize.go (nil in production) gives the test the encoder pointer, and the test holds a weak pointer and asserts that it becomes nil after GC. Exact proof, but a test-only hook lives in production code.

rationale: The signal is 42 MB against a limit of 8 MB in a test that runs before the parallel tests, so the heap check is not fragile. A test-only hook in the encode path is permanent code for a small gain in proof strength.
decision: Cache-absence check plus coarse live-heap limit after GC. No test hook in production code.

title: Clarify the Q5 follow-up
question: Q5 answer was 'A (file a follow up)'. Option A had no GitHub issue. Which one is meant?

options.text: Deferred item in this task's files only.
Deferred item plus a GitHub issue that I open after the implementation, with the title and body shown to the maintainer first.

rationale: The words 'file a follow up' read as a request for an issue. An issue is public, so I confirm before I create it.
decision: Deferred item plus a GitHub issue. Title and body shown to the maintainer before creation.
